Theorem
[elliptic estimates for ancient kappa-solutions] Source: cao-zhu 1. Theorem 6.4.3\group Three-Dimensional Ancient Kappa-Solutions There exist a positive constant $\eta $ and a positive increasing function $\omega :\quad [0,+\infty )\rightarrow (0,+\infty )$ with the following properties. Suppose we have a three-dimensional ancient $\kappa $-solution $(M,g_{ij}(t)),-\infty <t\le 0,$ for some $\kappa >0$. Then

  • for every $x,y\in M$ and $t\in (-\infty ,0]$, there holds

    \[ R(x,t)\le R(y,t)\cdot \omega (R(y,t)d_t^2(x,y)); \]

  • for all $x\in M$ and $t\in (-\infty ,0]$, there hold

    \[ |\nabla R|(x,t)\le \eta R^\frac {3}{2}(x,t)\; \mbox{ and }\; \left|\frac{\partial R}{\partial t}\right|(x,t)\le \eta R^2(x,t). \]

Proof

↗ thm:cz-local-volume-growth-curvature-estimate \sketch Universal noncollapsing, Harnack, and local volume-growth curvature control give the comparison function $\omega $. Shi estimates then give the spatial and temporal derivative bounds \cite{P1}.

□
